## Second sighting — the recurrence condition this card set for itself is met

This card said: *"Recorded as a **proposal** for the flaky-signature ledger, not an entry in it. If it
recurs, that is the second data point that makes it a confirmed flaky."* It recurred, 30 hours later,
on a different PR. ⛔ Evidence only — no label, no grading, no state change; that stays with triage.

| | first sighting (this card) | second sighting |
|---|---|---|
| PR evicted | #9365 (`packages/cli` only) | **#9775** (`packages/cli` + regenerated i18n bundles) |
| queue build | [32049971906](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/32049971906), `Test Core (2/3)` | [32196793380](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/32196793380), **`Test Core (3/3)`** |
| suite result | `21 passed (21)` files / `334 passed (334)` tests | `21 passed (21)` files / **`337 passed (337)`** tests |
| errors | `Errors 1 error` | **`Errors 3 errors`** |
| originating file | `test/approval-resume-relation-expand.test.ts` | **same** |
| message | `EnvironmentTeardownError: [vitest-worker]: Closing rpc while "onUserConsoleLog" was pending` | **identical, ×3** |

Same package, same file, same message, zero failing tests both times, non-zero exit both times.

## What is new: a paired measurement of the load hypothesis

This card proposed that the race is "timing- and log-volume-dependent by construction, which is
consistent with it appearing in the full-suite queue build rather than in the PR-side affected-subset
run" — but had no way to test it, because #9365 never ran `app-showcase` PR-side.

#9775 **did**. `examples/app-showcase` was in scope for PR-side `Test Core (2/3)` and for the queue's
`Test Core (3/3)`, so the identical diff ran the identical suite twice, ~20 minutes apart:

| | PR-side (head `cff1dd33c`) | queue-side (merge `f798a332`) |
|---|---|---|
| files / tests | 21 / **337 passed** | 21 / **337 passed** |
| errors | **none** — no `Errors` line, no `ELIFECYCLE` | **3** → `ELIFECYCLE` → exit 1 |
| duration | 25.99s | **72.74s** |
| transform | 23.52s | **65.69s** |
| import | 64.38s | **188.22s** |

⇒ The suite's own outcome is byte-for-byte the same verdict. The only thing that changed is how loaded
the runner was — transform and import each ~2.8–3× slower in the queue build, where the full suite runs
alongside it. **That is the load-dependence this card hypothesised, now measured rather than argued**,
and it is the strongest available evidence that no test and no product code is at fault.

⚠️ Still **not** established, exactly as this card already stated: that
`approval-resume-relation-expand.test.ts` is where the fault lies. Vitest's own wording is that the
file is where the rejection *originated*, not where it was thrown. Two sightings naming the same file
raises the prior, but the mechanism could equally be a shared showcase fixture that logs during
teardown.

## Cost, now that it is countable

Each occurrence evicts the PR **and rebuilds the full queue for everyone behind it**. The
merge-queue-triage bot reports **7 failed queue builds in the last 24h**; this signature is at least one
of them. #9775 is finished, verified, and green on every PR-side required check — it is unlanded
tonight solely because of this race.

## What I did not do

⛔ Did not re-queue #9775. The repo's own triage comment is explicit — 「修好前重排只会再烧一轮全队列」
— and with the flake now confirmed rather than suspected, a blind re-queue would spend a full-queue
rebuild to dodge a defect that is recorded and unowned. ⛔ Did not skip, quarantine, retry-wrap or
`--reporter`-silence anything.

Filed from the `domain:cli` seat (#6024) as its last action before going off shift.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #10375. Root-caused, not mitigated.

Reviewed against `origin/main`, not against the report. Flipped ready, auto-merge armed.

This card was dispatched with four outcomes I said I would accept, including *"unprovable in this container"* and *"it's upstream in vitest"*. It came back with the one nobody was entitled to expect: **a real defect in product code, reproduced, fixed, ablated, and measured paired.**

### The root cause, verified on `origin/main`

| claim | verified |
|---|---|
| `Plugin` declares `init()`, `start?(ctx)`, `destroy?()` | ✅ — and **no `stop()`** |
| `MessagingServicePlugin` has `async stop()` at `:382`, documented *"Stop the dispatcher loop + retention sweep on shutdown"* | ✅ — and **no `destroy()`** |
| nothing in `packages/core/src` calls `.stop()` | ✅ |

So the teardown body was correct and the intent was documented. **Only the name was wrong**, and the name is the whole contract.

⭐ The detail that makes this more than a typo: **`start?()` *is* on the interface.** The dispatchers therefore start, and never stop. A perfectly symmetric-looking `start`/`stop` pair where only one half is wired to anything — which is exactly why it survived review, and why no gate could see it. And `start()` `unref()`s both timers, so a long-lived host process still exits cleanly. It was invisible in production **by construction**, and could only surface somewhere that outlives its own teardown: a test worker.

### The mechanism explains the card's own unexplained measurement

Read out of installed vitest 4.1.10 rather than assumed:

1. A dispatcher tick fires **after the test file is over**, reads a delivery table through a driver the suite already disconnected, and `SqlDriver`'s console fallback warns.
2. `console.*` in a worker is an RPC — `sendLog` calls `rpc.onUserConsoleLog({...})` and **discards the returned promise**.
3. `execute()`'s `finally` awaits a **snapshot** of the pending set, then `$rejectPendingCalls` rejects anything created *after* that snapshot with `EnvironmentTeardownError`.
4. Nobody holds that promise ⇒ unhandled rejection ⇒ vitest fails a run on which every assertion passed.

> The width of the window is the duration of `rpcDone()`.

**That is the load-dependence this card recorded and could not explain.** The paired measurement on #9775 — identical diff, identical suite, 337/337 both times, clean PR-side and 3 errors queue-side with transform and import ~2.8–3× slower — is now a consequence rather than a coincidence.

### And it answers the question the card explicitly left open

The card was careful that vitest names where a rejection *originated*, not where the fault lies, and I passed that caution through. The dev did not claim the fault was in `approval-resume-relation-expand.test.ts`. Instead they measured **why it is always the file named**: instrumenting every `console.*` across the suite, that file makes **294 of the 348** console calls in the whole showcase run — the loudest by an order of magnitude, so it is where the RPC queue is deepest at teardown. Corroborated independently by vitest's own `--detectAsyncLeaks`, which names one file, and it is that file.

The correlation is explained without the fault being relocated. That is the distinction the card asked for.

### Reproduced before, measured after

Reproduced on a 4-vCPU container matching the runner profile, 4 concurrent showcase suites × 3 rounds, with a probe wrapping `rpc.onUserConsoleLog` — `AFTERALL` at t=37655, then eight `RPCSTART`s *after* it, then `RPCREJECT` carrying the exact signature.

Paired effect, 48 loaded runs each side, `dist` rebuilt between legs and the rebuild verified on disk:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| console calls after the file's own `afterAll` | **3** | **0** |
| RPCs never settled | **3** | **0** |
| RPC round-trips | 6574 | **3456** |

Both halves shrink — the late calls that arm the race, and the queue depth that widens its window.

**Ablation**: `destroy()` → `ABLATED_destroy()`, confirmed on disk by exact-text grep, yields `expected 94 to be 46` — **48 further delivery reads/writes in the 80 ms after a resolved `shutdown()`**. The defect, quantified, on a pin that can go red.

### Judgement calls I want on the record

- **`stop()` retained as a delegating alias.** It is public API of an exported class, and an embedder may have learned to call it directly *precisely because the kernel never did*. Removing it would have been the tidy choice and the wrong one.
- **The pin's pre-shutdown leg is a positive control**, called out as load-bearing: without it, a dispatcher that never started would pass vacuously.
- **A `vitest.config.ts` with one anchored `@objectstack/core` alias**, because a pin asserting a property of the *kernel's* teardown contract must run against this checkout's source, not a `dist` artifact.
- **Changeset, not `skip-changeset`** — `@objectstack/service-messaging` is published and its runtime behaviour changes. Correct, and the opposite call from the sibling cards this seat landed today.

### ⛔ Ledger promotion is yours, not mine

Per the signature-ledger rule this is a **human** action. The dev drafted a proposal and did **not** self-add it, exactly as instructed. It is in the PR body ready to promote, and it correctly records the residual risk: **the upstream amplifier is unfixed (#10374)**, so a recurrence in a *different* package is a new instance of the class, not a regression of this fix.

### Filed, not fixed here — all three correctly scoped out

- **#10371** — `plugin-reports` has the identical defect (5 timer sites, `stop()`, no `destroy()`), plus five further plugins whose `stop()` the kernel never calls.
- **#10373** — `approval-resume-relation-expand.test.ts` tears down driver-before-kernel.
- **#10374** — the upstream amplifier: any late `console.*` in any package can fail a green suite, and vitest's non-TTY default reporter never prints that output, so suites pay RPC round-trips for logs nobody reads.

⚠️ **#10371 is the one to look at next.** It is the same defect in another published plugin, found by the same reasoning, and it is unfixed on `main` right now.
